messages:
Alice Chen: FYI — after the automated KMS rotation for redwood-prod-1 completed, audit logs show decrypts from service-account etl-runner@redwood-prod that we did NOT expect to still be able to decrypt encrypted_blobs:sales-archive. Rotation finished ~1864126000. Can infra/security confirm? :warning:
Bob Patel: On it. I saw the rotation job succeed earlier (kms-rotation-bot posted). Pulling audit logs now. Do we have the exact log lines?
Alice Chen: Pasting an anonymized sample from Cloud Audit Logs:
```
{
  "protoPayload": {
    "authenticationInfo": { "principalEmail": "service-account:etl-runner@redwood-prod" },
    "methodName": "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt",
    "resourceName": "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/redwood-prod-1/cryptoKeyVersions/3",
    "requestMetadata": { "callerIp": "35.199.12.45" }
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-04-11T02:13:12Z"
}
```
Alice Chen: That Decrypt call is AFTER the rotation timestamp and the key version matches the new version.
Carol Nguyen: Hmm — last week's IAM role cleanup (PR #789) changed how we grant kms:Decrypt — it switched some services from resource-scoped grants to a role attached at project level for easier management. Might have widened scope unintentionally.
Dmitri Ivanov: Can we link PR diff? If so we should short-circuit: revert that role change or add a deny on the sales-archive resource until we confirm.
Bob Patel: Found PR: https://git.internal/rw/infra/PR/789 — yep, they moved decrypt permission into roles/cloudkms.decrypter at project scope for service-accounts/*-sa.
Sarah Lopez: This SA is used by the nightly ETL into analytics. We definitely don't want it decrypting sales-archive. That data is restricted.
Alice Chen: Immediate mitigation proposal: 1) remove roles/cloudkms.decrypter binding from project for etl-runner SA, 2) grant a narrowly scoped decrypt only to keys needed by ETL, 3) rotate any exposed ciphertexts if needed. Agree?
Carol Nguyen: +1. Also add an explicit Deny policy for sales-archive to ensure a short-term fail-safe while we investigate.
Dmitri Ivanov: I'll open a revert PR to reapply the resource-scoped grants and get CI to run.
Bob Patel: Doing step 1 now. Revoking project-level binding for service-account:etl-runner@redwood-prod -> applied.
kms-rotation-bot: rotation completed for redwood-prod-1 at 1864126000 (automated).
Alice Chen: After revoke, can audit logs confirm no further decrypt calls from that SA?
Bob Patel: Running query: `resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:etl-runner@redwood-prod AND timestamp>"2026-04-11T02:00:00Z"` — will report back in 2m.
Bob Patel: Query result: one decrypt at 2026-04-11T02:13:12Z (the one we saw) and no new ones since revoke at 02:22:40Z.
Sarah Lopez: Good. Next: data owner (product compliance) wants a timeline and impact list. I can draft. We should also notify legal/compliance.
Alice Chen: Agreed. Action items we're tracking: [P0?] Not sure on severity — access to restricted archive is bad. For now: 1) Incident channel #incidents/privileged-access, 2) Revert PR (#789) + narrow grants (Dmitri), 3) Add explicit deny on sales-archive (Carol), 4) Rotate any keys/ciphertexts if audit shows plaintext exposure (Bob/Alice), 5) Full audit query and share timeline (Sarah).
Dmitri Ivanov: Revert PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/infra/PR/804 — tagging sec and oncall.
Carol Nguyen: Adding deny rule via org policy now. Will post policy diff once applied.
Alice Chen: Filing a short incident report and risk classification. If compliance wants escalation, we'll move to SEV-1. For now marking as SEV-2 and monitoring. :eyes:
Sarah Lopez: I'll notify Compliance and Legal with initial findings and ETA for full report.
Bob Patel: Confirmed no further decrypts post-mitigation. Closing immediate blast radius. Will follow up with key rotation verification and replay logs.
Alice Chen: Thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread and #incidents/privileged-access. We'll reconvene after the audit results.
